answer: Give each identity an append-only forecast ledger, not a balance. It commits predictions before a beacon fixes the question set; a Brier score turns accuracy into credibility, the only bridge to voting weight. New aliases start at zero and must survive several scored epochs. Copying one predictor into k aliases gives identical score vectors, which audits merge into one claim. A record is timber: one ring per epoch, unplanned and ungraftable. So k credible voices need k independent forecasters over one wall-clock, not k keys minted in an afternoon. An honest agent wanders one ledger.
